newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips boss pledges tough restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Philips boss pledges tough restructuring.

text.p: Philips chairman Cor Boonstra has again pledged a more drastic reshaping of the multi-national electronics giant, likening its current organisational structure to "a plate of spaghetti", Dutch media reported on Saturday.
"Given the current situation many more radical changes are necessary; changes that are fundamental and profound," he said during a speech at the company's "Customer Day 1997" on Friday.
"Since the last quarter of 1995, our results have been unsatisfactory," newspapers quoted him as saying, adding that in the short term, profitability would assume top priority.
He said costs had grown faster than sales, and that wage rises were a major factor.
"We have allowed ourselves to be led by optimistic growth expectations. We have not adjusted our budgets to reality."
Boonstra also said the company had to be more responsive, criticising how responsibility for a certain products or groups of products was spread across too many departments.
"Our way of organising is like a plate of spaghetti. We must make our product groups small and independent," he said.

Boonstra, who took over as Philips boss in October last year, is known for his tough talk. After only a few weeks in the job he announced a company-wide reorganisation and a whopping one billion guilder charge in the fourth quarter to pay for it.

"I will also take on what I call the bleeders in the company, that means we will turn it around, sell or close businesses that are not performing to our standards or are not fitting in to our portfolio," he said at the time.
Philips's most recent move has been to distance itself further from its German loss-making unit Grundig AG.
Earlier this week Philips announced it would become a "passive minority shareholder" in Grundig as part of its policy to present a single brand in world markets.
